The past, present and future of PN

After 18 months in power, this Monday will in all likelihood herald the demise of the Perikatan Nasional (PN) government. As we know PN is a coalition of different factions: Bersatu, UMNO-BN, PAS, Azmin's 'geng kartel' from PKR, and Sarawak's GPS. Ideologically speaking, PN is but a hollow shell with no history nor common struggle shared between them. It is effectively a marriage of convenience in which each party has its own different agendas, motivation, and aspiration, but are forced together primarily by a common lust for power. However, while it remains easy to dismiss all of PN as selfish backstabbing party-hoppers, a detailed analysis of the factors and circumstances contributing to why and how PN managed to wrest power from Pakatan Harapan (PH) is warranted, if only to serve as a reminder for ourselves against such dastardly schemes in the future. Here we dissect the role of each party and biggest players in the establishment of PN, their current performance in government, and in the face of impending doom, what the future holds for them.

1. Bersatu
In my view the biggest culprits, who betrayed their PH friends. Their main concern was losing the Malay Muslim sentiments, being perceived as kowtowing too much to DAP and the liberals. Efforts were made to address this during PH, including organising a Konvensyen Melayu and extending olive branches to PAS and UMNO leaders (which further agitated the urban liberals and non-Malays, drawing more radical responses, thus perpetuating the cycle). Also, according to Bersatu leader Wan Saiful Wan Jan in his article justifying Bersatu's betrayal, PH's mistake was they focused too much on institutional reform and not enough on welfare issues. It's worth noting Wan Saiful was, and still is, PTPTN chairman and one of the original authors of PH's election manifesto, the same one he called "focused too much on institutional reform and not enough on welfare issues". 

Bersatu was also deeply triggered by PH member parties' ultimatum on the Mahathir-Anwar succession issue. Clearly they don't want Anwar to ever become premier, despite the wishes of the rakyat who voted for PH and Bersatu in the first place. Little by little, the party increasingly felt that the grass could be greener on the other side. A pact with UMNO-PAS was secretly made to "save" the Malay populace, and simultaneously block Anwar's path. They believed Mahathir could then rule in peace with a full Malay mandate, except that Mahathir himself opposed the move and insisted on honouring his allegiance to PH. In the end, Mahiaddin had to do. All this is of course ironic because Bersatu were an integral part of the "failed" PH govt, among them Mahiaddin as Home Minister and Redzuan Yusof of the kereta terbang fame. In essence, PH's successes were their successes, and PH's failures were their failures. To see Bersatu leaders now taking pot shots at PH feels quite.. bizzarre.

At this point we also need to account for the frogs from UMNO who joined Bersatu after GE-14, like Hamzah Zainuddin who was instrumental in bringing down PH. Another frog, Mustafa Mohamad or Tokpa, so-called honourably left for Bersatu because he cannot accept UMNO colluding with PAS (Khairy Jamaluddin even blamed party president Zahid for this - "this is on you!", he said then) but now he's a minister in the PN government with, yep, PAS. And so is Khairy, for that matter. What puzzles me though is how Bersatu members nationwide from the grassroots up, save from a small few loyal to Mahathir and PH, wholeheartedly embraced this act of betrayal. 

But the party-hopping plot does not stop there. During the PH government, UMNO division stalwarts jumped ship to Bersatu in droves to save their political careers. Eager to appease their new political masters, they rinsed their hands of UMNO, who was left for dead. I know that in universities, the same hands working to push UMNO narratives to students were now the ones blocking UMNO student activities, and promoting Bersatu instead. But when PN assumed power, suddenly these rats scuttled back to UMNO as if nothing happened. UMNO and Bersatu is interchangeable as if one is merely changing clothes. Bersatu, originally envisaged to be free of money politics, a clean and activism-rooted alternative to UMNO, is now a shadow of its former self. It competes for the same voter demographic as UMNO, but offers nothing new or different. Maybe now it's time to just disband, change their clothes, and rejoin UMNO. 

2. PKR Defectors
11 MP's in total, led by Azmin Ali and Zuraida Kamaruddin. Their motivation is the murkiest here. Azmin's obsession with stepping out of Anwar's shadow ultimately cost the PH government. He brings MP's like Saifuddin Abdullah, Kamaruddin Jaafar, Edmund Santhara and Rashid Hasnon who are seemingly clean and have no skeletons in their closet, but internally must despise Anwar. One account I heard was they resented that their lobbying for ministerial positions went unheeded by Anwar. Indeed, many of them obtained cushy minister or deputy minister jobs under PN, obviously courtesy of Azmin. But to go against your entire political principle, stab your PH friends in the back, betray your voters and decide to work with your biggest enemies, the so-called corrupt and racist-laden UMNO, that really takes the cake. To Amanah and DAP, Azmin & Co.'s treachery must have hurt the most. Many of them have been fighting on the same side for 20 years. Unlike Bersatu, they had no prior issues of pro-Malayness and never had beef with any Amanah or DAP ministers or MP's. Indeed, it was then-Foreign Minister Saifuddin Abdullah who was responsible for the ICERD and Rome Statute fiascos which provided so much ammo for the UMNO and PAS bases. For this brilliant work he is now rewarded with overseeing the PN communications and propaganda ministry, working with, yep, PAS. 

Anyhow, a big question mark that hangs over this group is their political identity. For 20 years they are known to be pro-reform, pro-integrity, certainly never race-based. After leaving PKR, like homeless animals they were forced to look for shelter. Eventually Azmin et al. were taken in (or just tolerated?) by Bersatu, and party posts were created especially to accommodate them. A "non-Malay affiliate" membership was even created just to induct Edmund Santhara into Bersatu. Arguably, this group is taking the biggest gamble of all: if PN falls they will most likely be the biggest losers, having alienated their voters, inciting the wrath of the rakyat, and losing crucial grassroot support. The incompetent policies of the PN government must not have helped either. Ultimately, this group looks to have sacrificed their long-term survival for some myopic short-term gains. Azmin is probably the most hated man in Malaysia right now, while it's hard to see Santhara on a Bersatu ticket winning any votes in his Segamat constituency. 

3. UMNO
Oh, hindsight is a wonderful thing. Who could've predicted when Zahid Hamidi and friends decided to turn up en masse at the Sheraton Hotel to support the new PN government, he was effectively instigating civil war within UMNO. To be fair Mahiaddin was clever enough to realise this, and so cherry-picked his UMNO MP's to become ministers and deputies. Some others got cushy GLC positions, while he veered well away from the rest. That started an indelible rift within the party. Zahid probably had high hopes his and Najib's corruption cases will eventually be thrown out, but that I guess is too much of a risk for Mahiaddin. Nonetheless, like a greedy animal UMNO wanted more, and demanded more. Johor and Perak state governments fell to them. Musa Aman and Tengku Adnan got off scott-free from their corruption cases. Ismail Sabri was elevated to Deputy PM. Muafakat Nasional with PAS is all but dead (more on that later). Unsatiated still, and reflecting on the widening rift and jealousy between the UMNO haves and have-nots, and widespread grassroot sentiments who feel Bersatu has turned into UMNO's biggest threat, Zahid finally withdrew their support. Overall, a failed experiment that leaves UMNO in an arguably worse state than 18 months ago.  

However, fate is not finished with them yet. A daring and outrageous manouver, provided everything else falls into place in the next few days, could see UMNO spectacularly wresting back the PM post through Hishamuddin Hussein or Ismail Sabri and leading the country again. Unlikely? Yes, similarly unlikely as Mahiaddin emerging to be PM from the Sheraton fiasco.

4. PAS
The proverbial whore of Malaysian politics. The least deserving but the most smug party to take a seat in the government's table, giddy to finally usurp their hated Amanah rivals even if it means sneaking through the backdoor. The delusional kingmaker who spread their legs first to Najib, then to Mahathir, then finally to Mahiaddin. The hypocrites jeering Amanah and PKR for working with DAP, then without a trace of irony helped MCA's Wee Jeck Seng win the by-election in Tanjung Piai. The party with the most useless and despised chain-smoking, truck-riding, barefaced-lying, victim-insulting Menteri Besar in Kedah history. The disgraced Law Minister Takiyuddin Hassan lying to our Agong. The religion-boinkers using arwah Adib, sijil UEC and RUU355 to win Malay support, but doing f**k-all about those issues in their one and a half years in 'Kerajaan Melayu Islam'. The disgusting serial cheater of their Muafakat Nasional (MN) spouse UMNO with the more sexy but decidedly dumber chick called Bersatu, but desperately trying to convince her to allow for polygamy. Halaluna wa haramukum. Good riddance. 

5. GPS
Perhaps the only member I can empathise with in this wretched PN coalition, and the only real kingmakers at play. Similar to Warisan in Sabah, I respect that they prioritise Sarawak's interests first and foremost, and prefer to play it close to the chest, observe the Semenanjung parties duking it out, before backing the one most likely to win. For GPS, political stability is of utmost importance. Therefore I do not begrudge them supporting PN, in much the same way they supported PH after GE-14. That doesn't mean though PH won't contest against them in the next elections. Whatever it is, expect some more interesting moves from GPS in the coming days. 

Conclusion
A final takeaway message is that even though all parties have their own reasons, on their own they would not have dared to venture forth, establish PN and usurp the then government. Bersatu-UMNO-PAS alone would not have the adequate numbers to form the government without help from Azmin's gang. And Azmin in return counted on Bersatu for sanctuary and minister posts for his chums after leaving PKR. In reality it was a joint effort in which each member depended on the other to survive the ordeal. And so in essence, all were culpable. May this sad episode in our nation's history serve as a lesson in politics to the future generation.

PAS-Umno Ties ‘Beyond Repair’ After Coup Talk

Allegations of a plot to topple Umno leaders have damaged ties between the party and PAS “beyond repair”, according to political scientist Ahmad Fauzi Abdul Hamid.

Fauzi, a professor at Universiti Sains Malaysia, said the alleged plot highlights the deep mistrust between Umno and its rivals PAS and Bersatu.

While there is no love lost between Umno and Bersatu, ties with PAS had been strained since Umno withdrew support for Muhyiddin Yassin’s government in August 2021.

PAS and Bersatu, Muhyiddin’s party, are allies in the Perikatan Nasional coalition, while PAS and Umno are nominal allies in Muafakat Nasional.

However, Umno and PAS candidates clashed in the recent state elections in Melaka and Johor, a clear signal that PAS was putting Perikatan Nasional ahead of the Muafakat Nasional.

Fauzi said the departure of former central committee member Khairuddin Aman Razali from PAS had a lot to do with his pro-MN stance, despite PAS president Abdul Hadi Awang clearly showing a preference for PN.

“So, it isn’t that surprising if there indeed exists a PAS-Bersatu plot to outflank Umno and reclaim the prime minister’s post before the next general election,” he said. “The plotters, if they exist, will see the move as saving PN from probable humiliation and even oblivion come GE15.”

The allegations of a plot arose from leaked documents purportedly the minutes of meetings involving PAS leaders and several prominent figures from Bersatu as well as Umno.

The minutes tell of a plan to expedite the sentences of top Umno leaders who are either on trial or have been convicted on charges such as criminal breach of trust, abuse of power and money laundering.

Several PAS leaders have since denied allegations of a plot, saying the documents were an attempt to damage the party’s relationship with Umno.

However, Council of Professors fellow Jeniri Amir said he believes Umno and PAS ties are not beyond repair, though electoral cooperation for GE15 was “out of the question” at this time.

“One thing is for sure, the leaked documents definitely aggravated the situation,” he said.

Anwar Ibrahim ( Head of PKR = Parti Keadilan Rakyat = National Justice Party ) called a press conference in KL yesterday morning (Wednesday 23/09/2020) n announced that he had now obtained a “strong, overwhelming,convincing” majority to overthrow the present  Moo ( = Muhiyiddin ) Govt. 

Anwar n wife ( Wan Azizah = former DPM).  had sought n had been granted an audience with the Agong. Unfortunately, the Agong had to be hospitalised at IJN (=institut Jantung Negara = National Heart Institute) , KL. So, the audience will now only take place after the Agong  is discharged from IJN. 

So far, all DAP (Lim Guan Eng, former Finance Minister) and Amanah (Mat Sabu, former Defence Minister) have announced that their Parties will b entirely behind Anwar. On Moo’s side, PAS (the Islamic Party) has announced that it would support Moo. Also, some members from UMNO n Moo’s present Perikatan Nasional/PN (National Alliance Party) 

Mahathir (now head of his newly- formed Pejuang Party)  has not said anything yet. But Anwar has left the door open for Mahathir. He has also welcomed Moo to work with the new Govt  when it is formed. 

Anwar, while reiterating that Malaysia is a predominantly Malay majority country, has also firmly stated that Malaysia must be inclusive of all the races n religions.  

MY COMMMENTS
—————————

1. With a majority of  only 2 or 3 members, it was always been expected that Moo’s PN Govt could topple any day. 

2. Moo has had to walk a tightrope to carefully keep the support of the other Parties that back him, esp of UMNO (Najib n gang) n PAS ( the Islamic Party, led by Hadi n his gang), both of whom had much earlier entered into a separate political alliance, Muafakat Nasional/MN ( = National Consensus/Compact). Moo n PN were never part of this MN. 

Hence, the power behind the throne has always been seen to b UMNO n PAS ie the Najib n Hadi gangs. Moo could not do anything without the support of both these gangs. But he did try to build up his own support  by the distribution of political posts, CLC posts, COVID assistance packages etc but it did not have the impact he might have desired. Instead, public opinion built up against him. 

3. If Anwar’s claim is accepted by the Agong, then Anwar would become the next PM. He has not named anyone else for other posts but, in response to the media yesterday, he categorically excluded  his wife Wan Azizah as the DPM. 

4. If  Anwar’s claim is not accepted by the Agong for whatever reason or if the Agong decides that it may b in the best interest of the country to end the political uncertainties that have bedevilled Malaysia for some time now, he may yet decide to dissolve Parliament ( he is the only one who can decide this).  In such an event, the country will go into a general elections soon. 

5. The focus of the country today is on the State Assembly elections in Sabah two days from now, on Saturday 26/09/2020. 

All the top personalities from Peninsular Malaysia on both sides of the political divide have gone on an active campaign trail in Sabah, including Moo, Lim Guan Eng  n others. 

The local campaigns  have been very anti- Peninsular Malaysia. 

The Party n personality who seems to command the highest  support is Shafie Apdal, the Chief Minister who heads the Warisan Plus Party. Shafie also had held various Federal posts at the Ministerial n other levels in the past. Shafie’s  call for Sabah to be given it’s proper economic rights n dues in Malaysia  n also his desire to build a Sabah inclusive of all races n religions has won widespread  appeal in Sabah n also resonates well in Peninsular Malaysia. 

If Shafie wins, he n his Party will certainly support Anwar. 

It is noteworthy to recall that in the midst of the recent political debacle in Malaysia, following Mahathir’s resignation as PM,  Shafie Apdal was identified by Mahathir as a possible candidate for the post of the next PM. 

6. This Saturday’s  Sabah State elections wlll certainly have strong ripples all over Malaysia ( including Sarawak) n could well b a game changer in the politics of Malaysia in the days ahead.
